summary: Campaigns for cage-free egg commitments from companies in Türkiye (Kafessiz Türkiye). A re-implementation of Animal Charity Evaluators' 2026 cost-effectiveness sheet: hens in new, in-progress and earlier commitments and in Migros' new cage-free supply, from ÇHKD's 2024–2025 spending plus the accountability work still to come.

sections.title: Benefits: new cage-free commitments
sections.explainer: ACE counts hen-years: the hens in each group of commitments, times the years ÇHKD brought the change forward, discounted for the wait until it takes effect and for later years counting less.

sections.title: Costs
sections.explainer: ÇHKD's spending on the programme in 2024 and 2025 with its share of running costs, plus what it expects to spend holding companies to these commitments.

sections.title: Cost/benefit
sections.explainer: ACE's bottom line: SADs averted per dollar for the cage-free programme, the only one it modelled (55% of ÇHKD's current work).

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: charityevals adjustments on top of ACE's model.

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for every animal model, not ACE's. Ambitious Impact's suffering-adjusted days (SADs) count each species' pain as a share of a person's, using its own species weights. Here those weights come out and Rethink Priorities' estimates go in, so every species is counted in days of a chicken's disabling pain. How a chicken's suffering compares with a person's is the one animal slider, under Your values.

rows.label: Hens covered by new commitments (already met)
rows.explainer: ÇHKD's count of the hens in commitments it won in 2024–2025 that companies have already met.

rows.label: Hens covered by new commitments (in progress)
rows.explainer: Hens in commitments won in 2024–2025 that companies have yet to meet.

rows.label: Hens in a new cage-free supply in Migros (not covered by a commitment)
rows.explainer: ÇHKD worked with the supermarket chain Migros to grow its cage-free supply. ACE treats this like a fulfilled commitment, discounted below for supply that may not last without one.

rows.label: Hens covered by commitments from before 2024 met in 2024–2025
rows.explainer: Older commitments that companies met during the evaluation window; ÇHKD's accountability work gets part of the credit (below).

rows.label: SADs averted per hen-year
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: a hen-year moved from a battery cage to cage-free reads the shared figure (Suffering-adjusted days per animal, under Data), as in every model crediting the same change. ACE's 2026 figure is 17.9 SADs per hen lifetime (3.5 to 34), divided by a 1.5-year laying life: 11.93 per hen-year, kept as the evaluator's. ACE's 2026 SADs reweight pain intensities (AIM found higher pain levels were overweighted before), so they are not comparable with the 2024 SADs the shared figure is built on.

rows.label: Years of impact (years the transition was brought forward)
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: reads the shared "Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway", like every model that credits a won reform. ACE's own figure, 15 years (8 to 30, from the Turkish industry's lack of progress on its own), is kept as the evaluator's.

rows.label: Years to implementation
rows.explainer: From ÇHKD's commitment data: many small commitments are met within one or two years, the larger ones take longer. Enters the discount for the wait below.

rows.label: Total number of hen-years impacted including discounts
rows.formula: (hens_fulfilled + hens_pre2024 * share_pre2024 + hens_migros * (1 - migros_discount) + hens_in_progress * fulfilment) * credit * time_discount * years_of_impact
rows.explainer: Each group of hens times its share of the credit, over the years brought forward, discounted. ACE's best-guess column multiplies by the full years of impact (its bound columns subtract the years to implementation); kept as ACE wrote it.

rows.label: Annual discount rate
rows.explainer: Your discount rate (Timing, under Your values). ACE's 2026 models all use 1.4% a year.

rows.label: Discount factor (wait until implementation, then the years of impact)
rows.explainer: The average discount over the years of impact, after waiting the years to implementation. ACE's sheet holds the result as a typed number (0.872); this row rebuilds it from the years and the rate, and gives ACE's value exactly.

rows.label: Share of responsibility for this achievement
rows.explainer: ACE: ÇHKD seems to be the only group working on this in Türkiye and was the only one contacting the companies. Who caused a win is a judgment, so filed as one; the range down to 70% is ours. ACE's sheet doesn't multiply by this row (it is 100%); here it is the credit used with "Credit by share of resources" off.

rows.label: ÇHKD's share of the resources all groups spent winning these commitments
rows.explainer: Ours. With "Credit by share of resources" on, a win is shared by what each group put into it. ACE finds ÇHKD the only group pressing these companies; international Open Wing Alliance campaigns touch a few multinationals among them. Our judgment: 90%, 70% to 100%.

rows.label: Credit for the commitments
rows.explainer: ACE's responsibility (100%) by default; with "Credit by share of resources" on, ÇHKD's share of the resources behind the wins.

rows.label: Probability that companies stick to their commitments
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: reads the shared share of cage-free commitments companies keep, as every model crediting a cage-free pledge does. ACE's own 70% (50% to 90%; many of ÇHKD's commitments are small) is kept as the evaluator's. Applies to the commitments still in progress.

rows.label: Share of impact from the implementation work for commitments won before 2024
rows.explainer: How much ÇHKD's 2024–2025 accountability work contributed to older commitments being met. ACE's credit share, kept in both views.

rows.label: Future accountability spending as a multiple of the spending so far
rows.explainer: ÇHKD expects to spend about as much again holding companies to these commitments as it spent winning them. ACE's bounds: twice as much (conservative) to a fifth (optimistic).

rows.label: Additional costs required for future work on the commitments won in 2024 and 2025
Discount for increased cage-free supply not covered by a commitment
rows.explainer: Supply without a public commitment could slip back; ACE takes off 12.5% (5% to 20%).

Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Advocacy is mostly people, so staff pay is usually most of the budget. We haven't seen this charity's breakdown; the default is the same guess we use for other animal advocacy groups. Range is ours.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable for-profit jobs
rows.explainer: Campaigners, researchers and negotiators could typically earn considerably more in comparable for-profit roles. Range is ours.

Share of the full cost paid by cash donations
How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far
rows.explainer: Çiftlik Hayvanlarını Koruma Derneği's own figure (shared data, next_dollar): how much its next dollar does compared with the past average this estimate starts from, from how much room it has for more money, what the next dollar buys and how well it is run (docs/normalization.md 2.10). The evaluator view keeps {{row:marginal_vs_past_average:evaluator}}.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): the charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work.

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar you give
rows.explainer:
Times the charity's share of the good that others carry out (mobiliser_share).

A marginal dollar is counted at the share of the past average you set (row above).

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar you give: chickens
Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give: chickens
rows.explainer: In our view the SADs per hen-year are the shared figure, built with the hen weight inside the 2024 SADs (46% of a person's); taking that weight out leaves days of a chicken's disabling pain. A chicken counts as 1 here by definition; how a chicken's suffering compares with a person's is the chicken slider. The evaluator view keeps Ambitious Impact's weight, so ACE's own result reproduces.

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give
rows.explainer: Days of disabling pain spared, counted as a chicken's. The headline converts this into years of healthy life with the chicken slider and the healthy hours lost per day of disabling pain.
